title: A Watchman and the Fall of Jerusalem
overview: Ezekiel is given his role as a watchman again, God pleads with the people to turn and live, and news arrives that Jerusalem has fallen.

parts.label: The watchman's duty (vv. 1-9)
parts.note: A city lookout who sees an enemy coming must sound the alarm; if people ignore it, the fault is theirs, but if he stays silent, he shares the blame. God applies this picture to Ezekiel, who must pass on God's warnings whether or not anyone listens.

parts.label: Turn and live (vv. 10-16)
parts.note: Weighed down by guilt after disaster, the exiles ask how they can go on living, and God answers that he takes no pleasure in anyone's death but wants them to turn back and live. What counts is the direction a person takes now, shown in concrete acts like returning what was taken as security for a loan or what was stolen.

parts.label: Is God fair? (vv. 17-20)
parts.note: The people complain that this way of judging is unfair, perhaps because it lets the wicked off or because past goodness offers no safety. God turns the charge back on them: each person will be judged by their own path.

parts.label: News that the city fell (vv. 21-22)
parts.note: A survivor reaches the exiles in Babylon months after Jerusalem's fall, as earlier foretold, and the exact timing has puzzled scholars. Ezekiel had been kept largely silent until then, and the evening before the messenger came, God freed him to speak again.

parts.label: The survivors' false confidence (vv. 23-29)
parts.note: People left in ruined Judah reason that if one man, Abraham, received the land, so many of them surely own it now. God answers that they break his basic laws, such as eating meat with the blood still in it (blood stood for life, which belonged to God), worship idols, rely on violence and commit adultery, and he warns of sword, wild animals and disease.

parts.label: Admired but not heeded (vv. 30-33)
parts.note: The exiles gather eagerly to hear Ezekiel, but treat him like a singer of love songs with a lovely voice, enjoying the performance while changing nothing. When his words come true, they will realize a real prophet was among them.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the warning that a righteous person who turns to evil will die (vv. 12-13, 18) speaks of eternal salvation, and so whether it can be lost, or of life and death in this world under the law given to Israel.
think: Have you ever enjoyed listening to someone's words while quietly having no intention of letting them change you, and what made that possible?
